Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: eight-frame animation key-pose atlas derived from the input portrait.
The attached image is the EXACT approved reference, not merely inspiration. Create an atlas of 8 full copies of this same portrait: exactly FOUR columns by TWO rows, eight EQUAL cells, no gutters, no borders, no labels. Every cell must have the reference image's exact aspect ratio and composition. Read poses left to right then second row. Show the ENTIRE scene in every cell, never crop feet, head, chair or artwork relative to the original. Lock the camera, scale, character position, face profile, short fuzzy hair, hoodie, clothes, white earbud cord, all fixed objects and background. Vary ONLY the specified hands, wrists and forearms, with anatomically natural adult male hands and smooth hoodie sleeves.
Keep the flat near-black silhouette visual language, vivid original background color and softly photographic edge. No visible fingers drawn inside the black silhouette, no skin tones, no outlines, no text. Fingers should be readable through the outer contour. Keep hand size and arm proportions matching the original portrait. No tiny monkey fists, no bulky bunches of fabric, no scalloped or ruffled cuffs.
Make eight distinct successive poses of a SMALL, BELIEVABLE action that form a closed animation loop: the elbow/upper-arm joint remains attached to the original torso in the exact same position while the wrist and fingers articulate. Frame 8 should lead naturally back to frame 1. Do not move the whole person, do not bend/warp objects, no ghosts or duplicate arms.
Action: The man ACTUALLY WRITES in the notebook on his lap. His naturally sized hand grips the pencil near its tip with thumb and index finger, like the exact original. Frames 1-4: the hand and forearm travel about 12–18 original-image pixels along the notebook's sloping top surface as he writes a few strokes; fingers and wrist change pose, the pencil tip stays on the paper. Frames 5-6: lift the pencil 3–5 pixels and return the hand left. Frames 7-8: lower the tip and begin the next stroke. The pencil moves WITH the hand. Preserve notebook, spiral edge and legs EXACTLY. Hand, loose smooth sleeve and forearm must remain the same size as the reference and attached to the existing elbow. Vivid original red backdrop, original three thought marks above his head remain fixed.

redCleanPlate:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Input image 1 is the edit target: the approved red and black silhouette portrait. Input image 2 is a magnified supporting reference of the writing hand and forearm.
Make a clean animation background plate of Image 1. Remove ONLY the writing hand, pencil, and horizontal lower forearm that extends left from the torso above the notebook. Fill their former area with the same perfectly matching red background. Preserve the notebook's diagonal spiral-bound top edge underneath, preserve the crossed legs and lap, preserve the upper arm and torso on the right. The man is simply missing his lower writing arm, for later animation compositing.
Keep ALL other pixels/composition as close as possible: exact same short fuzzy hair with no quiff, bowed head, hoodie, body, earbuds and white cord, black seat, three thought marks, rich red background, dimensions and framing. Do not redesign the scene. Do not move the notebook or figure. No new objects, no lettering. Full original 3:4 portrait composition.
